card: TASK LENGTH AI CAN FINISH · METR, JAN 2026

lines.text: Here's the part nobody explains properly.
In nineteen fifty-six, ten scientists asked for one summer to teach machines to think.
That summer lasted seventy years.
Then the gaps started closing. Decades. Years. Months.
On September the twenty-second, two labs shipped new models, about ninety minutes apart.
That's not a trend line. That's a launch ramp.
The same level of AI got a thousand times cheaper in three years.
So what do you do... when the floor starts moving?
Eighteen forty-eight. California. Gold.
Everyone ran for the rivers.
One guy, Sam Brannan, ran for the shovels.
Thirty-six thousand dollars in nine weeks. Without swinging a pick.
They saw a gold rush. He saw a supply chain.
card: EVERYONE ELSE: 'POSITIVE AND LARGE' · CLAY & JONES, 2008

lines.text: Right now, everyone's digging for the same gold. Apps. Agents. Startups.
Meanwhile, the takeaway round the corner is still handing up to thirty percent of every order to an app.
The shovel isn't the model. The shovel is knowing what it can do... and walking in the door.
So here's your homework, from one chip to another.
Find one thing the curve just made cheap. Sell it to someone who hasn't noticed yet.
See you on the curve.
